name: Bubonic plague (flea- and louse-borne, as in the Second Pandemic)

reproduction_number_range.source: Dean et al. 2018, PNAS: human-ectoparasite transmission explains the Second Pandemic's epidemics in European cities, with a basic reproduction number a little above one (about 1.3 to 1.5); not re-checked

transmissibility_per_day.source: A reproduction number of 1.4 divided by the infectious days

case_fatality.source: WHO plague fact sheet: bubonic plague untreated kills roughly 30 to 60 percent; not re-checked

immunity.source: Survivors are taken as immune for life; the literature on later waves in a recovering population is mixed and not re-checked

stage.incubating.source: Incubation of a few days (two to six); shape 4 is a middling spread around the mean

stage.infectious.source: Illness and infectious vector load last about a week to ten days before death or recovery; shape 2 is a broad spread

density_exponent.source: Heuristic inside the range Rader et al. 2020 supports (crowded cities see longer epidemics with larger attack rates; weaker than linear); vary across the ensemble
